headline: India warns against using tech for strategic one-upmanship, calls for inclusive AI governance
body: India’s UN Ambassador asserted that amid the rapid integration of AI into military and intelligence spheres, responsibility for the use of lethal autonomous weapons systems must always rest with humans
full_body:

India’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, during the UN Security Council high-level open debate on the theme, “Conflict Resolution in an Era of Rapid Technological Change”. Photo: X/X/@AmbHarishP.

India has voiced concern over the instrumentalisation of technology for strategic one-upmanship through export control and licensing regimes, calling out the tendency to treat countries of the Global South as mere consumers as it underscored that technological transformation must not deepen existing inequalities.

Addressing the Security Council’s high-level open debate on Maintenance of International Peace and Security on ‘Conflict Resolution in an Era of Rapid Technological Change’, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni said AI systems can inadvertently perpetuate biases related to gender, language and socio-economic background.

Delivered India's statement at the UN Security Council high-level open debate convened by Latvia. Speaking on the theme, "Conflict Resolution in an Era of Rapid Technological Change", I highlighted four key considerations: 1️⃣ Technology must remain human-centric and an instrument of peace 2️⃣ The application of emerging technologies in conflict settings must be responsible, human-centric, respect sovereignty, and adhere to international law 3️⃣ We must address threats posed by misuse of emerging technologies such as AI 4️⃣ Technological transformation must not deepen existing inequalities. We must address technology denial and the instrumentalisation of technology for strategic one-upmanship through export control and licensing regimes. Countries of the Global South should not be tested as mere consumers without any agency or stake in how emerging technologies such as AI are developed, regulated and deployed.

“We note with concern the emerging medium- and long-term trends of technology denial and the instrumentalisation of technology for strategic one-upmanship through export control and licensing regimes, and a tendency to treat countries of the Global South as mere consumers without any agency or stake in how emerging technologies such as AI are developed, are regulated and are deployed,” Mr. Parvathaneni said.

He emphasised that technology should serve humanity, strengthen international cooperation, and advance the cause of lasting peace.

headline: U.S. lawmakers raise alarm at FAA decision to deploy aviation AI tool nationally
body: U.S. Democrats, led by Representative Rick Larsen of Washington, the ranking member of the ⁠House Transportation Committee, criticised the “sudden expansion of a largely untested ⁠system”
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

A group of two dozen U.S. House Democrats on Tuesday raised serious concerns about the Federal Aviation Administration decision to deploy a new AI tool to assist air traffic controllers nationwide on November 10, days before a ⁠major system failure.

The FAA in September began using a new software-based AI tool system in the Washington area that uses predictive analytics to improve how flights are managed after awarding an $875 million, 12-year contract to Air Space Intelligence.

The Democrats, led by Representative Rick Larsen of Washington, the ranking member of the ⁠House Transportation Committee, criticised the “sudden expansion of a largely untested ⁠system” and asked the FAA to answer a series of questions by November 30. “We have yet to receive any substantive information proving the system was properly validated before its nationwide expansion,” the lawmakers wrote.

The system, dubbed Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories, or SMART, uses data to analyse airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, airspace conditions and operational constraints to predict traffic flows and identify potential conflicts before they occur.

The letter cited the nearly five-hour November 13 nationwide ground stop that led flights to be canceled for an estimated ⁠1.5 million passengers due to an FAA telecom issue.

“The federal government is dealing with a crisis of confidence,” the letter said. “Americans’ faith in the aviation system is shaken. The opacity and inconsistency with which the FAA has handled the SMART rollout threatens to further undermine that trust.”

headline: Why U.S. President Donald Trump believed he needed to get Jensen Huang back at Nvidia
body: U.S. President Donald Trump has intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, following his recent ouster
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

U.S. President Donald Trump saw little choice but to fight to reinstate Jensen Huang at AI behemoth Nvidia .

The president has staked the nation's economic growth on artificial intelligence, and worried Mr. Huang's ouster was not only tanking the stock market — but also risked putting the U.S. behind Beijing in the race for dominance in the field if Mr. Huang, widely seen by backers and critics as a generational talent in artificial intelligence, were to be poached by a Chinese firm.

And the president, a thrice-married man and real estate maven who has seen his own marital infidelity scrutinised in the press, bristled at Mr. Huang being ousted from the company he built because of extramarital affairs, including one with an executive at a Singapore-based company who U.S. officials suspect was a Chinese spy.

So Mr. Trump engaged in an extraordinary level of behind-the-scenes maneuvering to reinstate Mr. Huang, starting almost immediately after the CEO's fall from grace when he resigned on November 12 as reports trickled out about a trio of affairs.

The U.S. president stated plainly in a CNBC interview on Monday he used his considerable sway to get Mr. Huang his job back. “I spoke to them,” Trump said of the company's board of directors. “Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them.”

Monday's reinstatement was a remarkable turnaround by Nvidia's board, which had insisted days after Mr. Huang’s ouster that it was not considering such a move, even as Trump pushed for it and thousands signed an online petition calling for Huang’s return.

Sales of Grand Theft Auto VI generated a record with $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales, maker Rockstar Games said Friday (November 20, 2026), underscoring the enormous demand for the first new installment in the blockbuster series in 13 years.

The worldwide figure was based on company estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game launched. Rockstar also said in a release that it sold 32.5 million units prerelease, setting a record across platforms.

“We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you,” Sam Houser, Rockstar’s president and founder, said in a release.

Grand Theft Auto V released in 2013, generated $1 billion in retail sales in its first three days. It went on to become one of the bestselling video games of all time, accounting for more than 230 million of the franchise's more than 470 million units sold globally, according to publisher Take-Two Interactive.

Earlier Friday, market research firm Sensor Tower estimated GTA VI had generated $2.36 billion in revenue on approximately 24.6 million units sold. Rockstar's figures, released later in the day, were based on the company's own estimates of worldwide, day-one retail sales.

The standard edition of the game retails for around $80 in the U.S.

headline: This 2D rhythm platformer video game is an ode to India’s multiplicities
body: Suri: The Seventh Note by Tathvamasi Studios is set in a universe controlled by evil music. The game was launched in October
full_body:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Today's Cache Your download of the top 5 technology stories of the day.

The story of Suri: The Seventh Note, a 2D video game by Bengaluru-based Tathvamasi Studios, is set in a world corrupted by an evil version of music. Everything in this universe moves in tune with that nefarious sonic presence. The protagonist, Ajira, must find a fruit located at the centre of the island to save her mother from certain death. Soon, she realises her actions shall determine the fate of the island itself.

Suri: The Seventh Note is the brainchild of Glen Martin from Kochi, founder of Tathvamasi Studios, who is also the game director of the video. He is joined by Chitrak Srivastava, co-founder and the game’s art director. The game was launched on Playstation Store and Steam in October.

Glen, formerly a data scientist, found himself immersed in game-making during the pandemic. He began by making smaller games, with friends from different places joining him on a Discord server to help. “When we started to build the game, it was not meant to be a project. But once we realised its potential, we began to think about what could be unique about this game,” says Glen.

“At that point, I was playing a parry-focused combat game called Sekiro. It’s a very hard game, and I am not good at it. But then I saw a lot of streamers play the game skilfully, without even taking a single hit, and I realised that when the game is played at that level, it has a certain rhythmic quality to it,” he adds. “The sounds of the sword clinking, the jumps and movements, everything felt choreographed.”

This ultimately led him to turn Suri… into a rhythm platformer game.

Suri... is a mix of two different games: rhythm and platformer. Rhythm games are music-themed action games that assess a player’s sense of timing and metre, while platformers are a sub-genre where a main character moves through uneven terrain and suspended platforms.

headline: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
body: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics
full_body:

Updated - November 21, 2026 12:05 am IST - Washington, D.C., United States

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.

“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released Friday (November 20, 2026).

The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.

It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers $1 million for a solution to each.
